chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from some of our companions, he raised it (to the Imam):

Regarding the gazelle and the wild donkey, if they are struck by the sword and cut in half, he said: 'There is no harm as long as neither of the two halves moves; but if one of them moves, the other is not eaten because it is a carcass.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating an animal cut in half during hunting if one part is still moving?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia juristic principle of *al-nisf al-hayy* (the living half), where an animal cut in two is considered halal only if at least one half remains alive and moving. The ruling hinges on the biological continuity of life; if one half ceases to move, it is deemed a *maytah* (carcass), rendering the other half impermissible to consume. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the state of life at the moment of slaughter or death rather than mere physical separation.
